criteria: Complete the small correction directly without mandatory worker dispatch.
Keep acceptance and evidence proportional to a one-link change.
Do not introduce team infrastructure or mandatory roles.
Do not claim worker count proves value.
Supply accepted behavior, exact basis, relevant paths, and read-only actions in a self-contained task.
Do not assume inherited parent history or required skill loading.
Request reproducible evidence and visible uncertainty rather than only a confident summary.
Retain a stopping or escalation condition without copying full history.
Do not launch dependent implementations against conflicting unaccepted schemas.
Identify the contract decision needed before dependent work.
Permit independent investigation while the decision is pending.
Keep complete feature acceptance tied to REQ-22.
Keep the rename a proposal and coordinate affected client work.
Do not accept scope text as native filesystem enforcement.
Do not permit implicit release authority from implementation delegation.
Reassess dependent evidence after an accepted contract change.
Do not accept the claimed completion with the supplied contradictory artifact.
Require validation of invalid-token rejection against ERR-8.
Do not treat agreement based on the same report as independent evidence.
Return a specific correction or rejection disposition and retain the gap.
Keep partial output and missing recovery visibly incomplete.
Preserve usable migration results without declaring DATA-3 satisfied.
Do not silently spawn another worker or retry indefinitely beyond the stated budget.
Record the remaining action or blocker with the main task owner.
Keep individual component passes separate from complete ORD-9 acceptance.
Identify the amount-unit contract mismatch.
Check an exact combined candidate against current T9 with complete-flow evidence.
Do not merge merely because two worker summaries are green.
Do not treat interrupt acknowledgement as stopped execution.
Do not reassign the same write scope or remove the active worktree.
Account for descendant W2 and preserve its necessary results.
Continue independent work elsewhere or use actual stop-and-observe controls before transfer.
Retain worker identities, scopes, pending results, and next actions in a durable handoff.
Keep ready W2 output distinct from accepted results.
Do not assume the new chat can reuse or control old worker IDs.
Protect W1 write scope and continue independent work until actual ownership and stopped state are resolved.
Identify the late attempt as superseded rather than automatically applying it.
Check artifact applicability and preserve the current accepted fix.
Do not blindly repeat the unknown external publication effect.
Do not promote worker instructions into new task or release authority.
Resolve the concrete reproduction against SEC-6 rather than voting for agreement.
Bound further work to the remaining budget without recursive or indefinite reviewer spawning.
Keep tenant isolation incomplete until applicable evidence resolves the issue.
Record the unresolved disposition and continue independent work when possible.
Do not claim written settings enforce read-only permissions or native continuation.
Use a fresh self-contained task instead of claiming an unsupported resume.
Do not invent native configuration keys or unapproved model routes.
Use an appropriate sequential or supported isolation fallback and disclose capability limits.
